subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw adopt canonical readiness conditions, plugin readiness providers, and standard hosting profiles as supported core contracts?
rationale: The RFC adds public runtime semantics, configuration, plugin API, and continuing release-support commitments; automation can assess coherence but cannot authorize those product and compatibility choices.

options.title: Accept after compatibility review
options.body: Approve the upgrade semantics and support boundaries, require the planned runtime evidence, create the implementation issue, mark the RFC accepted, and then merge it.

options.title: Accept only the condition foundation
options.body: Adopt canonical core conditions and the compatible local projection first while deferring plugin providers and non-local hosting profiles to later proposals.

options.title: Decline core hosting profiles
options.body: Keep hosting-specific readiness composition downstream and avoid creating a new OpenClaw-owned support contract.

recommendation.title: Accept after compatibility review
recommendation.body: Approve the upgrade semantics and support boundaries, require the planned runtime evidence, create the implementation issue, mark the RFC accepted, and then merge it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main provenance spans Gateway readiness, event-loop behavior, health surfaces, and plugin registry evolution, which are the core contracts this RFC would change.
